mainTopic: שמואל and רבי יוחנן on ביטול רשות between courtyards and in a חורבה, and when nested courtyards can renounce
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof. שמואל's rule ('where they forbid each other but cannot make an עירוב, they cannot do ביטול רשות') refers to a נכרי who arrived on שבת, which explains רבי אלעזר's surprise at רבי יוחנן. רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching. אביי reminds him that he himself taught it on שמואל's rules: no ביטול רשות from one חצר to another, and none in a חורבה. רב יוסף had limited the first rule to side-by-side courtyards, allowing ביטול for courtyards one inside the other (זו לפנים מזו). When רב יוסף objects with שמואל's rule to follow the exact wording of the משנה, אביי shows that rule was said about the מבוי משנה. The גמרא then presents the full argument: רבי יוחנן allows ביטול רשות in both cases, and a צריכא explains why both cases had to be stated. אביי limits שמואל's rule to side-by-side courtyards. רבא says that even with nested courtyards, ביטול sometimes works and sometimes does not, depending on where the עירוב was placed and who forgot to join. The גמרא explains why ביטול fails in each case where both courtyards are forbidden, and its discussion of the remaining case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's rule must refer to a gentile who arrived on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל's teaching speaks about a נכרי who came on שבת. In that case the residents forbid each other but cannot make an עירוב, so they cannot do ביטול רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be talking about a case where the gentile arrived on שבת. And שמואל teaches: where people forbid each other but cannot make an עירוב, they cannot renounce their rights. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its reading of שמואל's teaching. It concludes that שמואל means a case where the נכרי showed up on שבת, so no ביטול רשות is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא ruled out the case of a נכרי who came on ערב שבת, because then they could simply rent from him before שבת. So the only case left is one where he arrived on שבת, when an עירוב can no longer be made. That means שמואל forbids ביטול רשות in such a case, which explains why רבי אלעזר was surprised at רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that… (introduces the only remaining explanation)
They forbid (each other from carrying)
They make an עירוב together
They renounce (their property rights) — ביטול רשות
Learn from this (a conclusion has been proven)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that ביטול רשות works only where an עירוב could have been made. That idea drives the rest of the discussion.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that the gentile arrived on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The case of arriving on ערב שבת was already rejected.

phrases.english: and it teaches: where they forbid each other but cannot make an eiruv,
they may not renounce their rights.
Learn from this.
phrases.notes: So that's the conclusion, and it explains why רבי אלעזר was surprised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the elimination argument on the previous amud (the ערב שבת case was rejected).
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל forbids ביטול רשות when the נכרי arrived on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's rule: אוסרין ואין מערבין — אין מבטלין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Where people forbid each other but an עירוב is impossible (the נכרי came on שבת), ביטול רשות does not work, according to שמואל.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he does not know this teaching of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I have not heard this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says this law is new to him. This sets up אביי's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף forgot much of his learning because of an illness, so his student אביי often reminded him of his own teachings. His statement here is not an attack on the law. It opens a short story in which the source of the teaching is traced back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: I have not heard it
A teaching / a halachic tradition

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not disagreeing with the law. He simply does not remember it, and the next lines show that he himself was the one who taught it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I have not heard this teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the teaching of שמואל that was just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not recognize this teaching.

steps.title: אביי reminds רב יוסף, citing שמואל on courtyards
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that he himself taught it. He taught it on שמואל's rule that there is no ביטול רשות from one חצר to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and you told it to us on this: שמואל said there is no renunciation of rights from one courtyard to another.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reminds his teacher that he taught this law himself. He identifies the teaching it was attached to: שמואל's rule about courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule means this: a person may give up his rights in his own חצר to the other residents there. He may not give up his rights in a different חצר to the people of that חצר. אביי quotes this rule as the base that רב יוסף once explained.

keyTerms.meaning: You (yourself) told it to us
And on this (statement)
Renouncing one's property rights so others may carry
From one courtyard to another

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You told it to us,
and it was on this that you told it to us,
as Shmuel said:
There is no renunciation of rights from one courtyard to another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's claim that he never heard the teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where did this teaching come from?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף himself taught it, explaining שמואל's rule אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר.

steps.title: שמואל: no renunciation of rights in a ruin
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's second rule: there is no ביטול רשות in a חורבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is no renunciation of rights in a ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, still reminding רב יוסף, quotes a second rule of שמואל that was said together with the first. If two houses share a ruin, neither can give up its rights there to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים set up ביטול רשות only for a normal courtyard, which is the usual case. A חורבה is not a regular living space, so this tool does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruin (an abandoned or destroyed building area)

phrases.english: And there is no renunciation of rights in a ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting שמואל's statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביטול רשות does not apply to a ruin.

steps.title: רב יוסף had limited שמואל's rule to side-by-side courtyards
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רב יוסף's explanation: שמואל's rule applies only to two courtyards next to each other with one opening between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us about it: When שמואל said there is no renunciation from one courtyard to another, we said this only about two courtyards with one opening between them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רב יוסף exactly what he had said: שמואל's courtyard rule has a limit. It covers only two side-by-side courtyards that share one doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case each courtyard also opens to the alleyway, so they do not really depend on each other. Each one can use its own exit. So one courtyard's residents cannot give up rights in the other courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: And you told us about it
We said this only in the case of…
A single opening between them

phrases.english: And you said to us about it:
When Shmuel said
there is no renunciation of rights from one courtyard to another,
we said this only
about two courtyards with a single opening between them.
phrases.notes: The two courtyards sit side by side, and each one also opens out to the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרְתְּ לַן עֲלַהּ: כִּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of שמואל's rule quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר applies only to two side-by-side courtyards sharing one opening.

steps.title: Inner and outer courtyards can renounce, since they forbid each other
steps.stepSummary: When one courtyard is inside the other, they forbid each other, so ביטול רשות is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one courtyard is inside the other, since they forbid each other, they may renounce their rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף's teaching ends with the exception. If the courtyards are nested one inside the other, ביטול רשות is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of the inner courtyard must walk through the outer one, so they forbid the outer courtyard's residents from carrying. Because they forbid each other, the system of ביטול רשות applies, and they may give up their rights. The rule is: where there is mutual forbidding (אוסרין זה על זה), there can also be ביטול.

keyTerms.meaning: One inside the other (inner and outer courtyards)
Since / because
They forbid each other from carrying

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: no ביטול רשות from one חצר to another, and none in a חורבה. רב יוסף limited the first rule to side-by-side courtyards. Courtyards one inside the other forbid each other, so they may do ביטול רשות.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's 'no ביטול from courtyard to courtyard' is not a blanket rule. It does not apply to nested courtyards, because they forbid each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the principle that ביטול רשות goes together with mutual forbidding. It is the 'teaching' that רב יוסף had forgotten.

phrases.english: But if one is inside the other,
since they forbid each other —
they may renounce their rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to the limitation in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Nested courtyards (זו לפנים מזו) forbid each other, so their residents may do ביטול רשות in favor of one another.

steps.title: רב יוסף questions whether he really said it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks how he could have limited שמואל's rule. He points out that שמואל said in עירובין we follow only the exact wording of the משנה, which says 'people of a courtyard' (one courtyard), not 'courtyards.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did I say such a thing in the name of שמואל? But שמואל said: In עירובין we have only what the wording of our משנה says. It says 'people of a courtyard,' and not 'people of courtyards'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is surprised by what אביי reported in his name, and he challenges it. He quotes another statement of שמואל that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows ביטול רשות only for 'people of a courtyard,' which is singular. If we stick to that exact wording, ביטול רשות should never work between two courtyards, even when one is inside the other. That clashes with the explanation in step 5–6, which allowed it for an inner and outer courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Did I say? (a question of surprise)
But didn't he say! (introduces a contradicting source)

keyTerms.term: אֵין לָנוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין אֶלָּא כִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָתֵנוּ
keyTerms.meaning: In עירובין we go only by the exact wording of our משנה
People of a courtyard (singular)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not doubting אביי's honesty. רב יוסף had forgotten his learning, and אביי often reminded him of what he once taught. Here he raises a real textual problem with that teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא אָמֵינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did I say this in the name of Shmuel?
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָנוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין אֶלָּא כִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָתֵנוּ —
phrases.english: In eiruvin we have only the wording of our Mishnah —
'people of a courtyard,' and not 'people of courtyards'!
phrases.notes: Since it says 'courtyard,' just one, giving up your rights only works within a single courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא אָמֵינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation attributed to רב יוסף in steps 5–6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ביטול רשות works between an inner and outer courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל requires following the משנה's singular wording, so ביטול רשות should never work between two courtyards.

steps.title: אביי explains where that statement was said
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רב יוסף taught the 'exact wording of our משנה' rule about a different משנה: an alleyway is to its courtyards like a courtyard is to its houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When you told us 'In עירובין we have only the wording of our משנה,' you said it about this: that an alleyway is to its courtyards like a courtyard is to its houses.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's challenge. He explains that the statement of שמואל belongs to a different topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'exact wording' rule was said about the משנה on מבוי. There it teaches that an alleyway needs courtyards (plural) with houses (plural) opening into it. It was never said about the ביטול רשות משנה, so it does not contradict the inner/outer courtyard explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: On this (about this other teaching)
An alleyway that courtyards open into
Like a courtyard to its houses

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of following the משנה's exact wording was said about the alleyway משנה, not about ביטול רשות. So רב יוסף's earlier explanation stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: When you told us

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָנוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין אֶלָּא כִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָתֵנוּ —
phrases.english: 'In eiruvin we have only the wording of our Mishnah' —
you said it to us about this:
that an alleyway to its courtyards is like a courtyard to its houses.
phrases.notes: Notice it says 'courtyards' and 'houses': an alleyway needs at least two courtyards, each with houses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the quoted statement to a different משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's 'exact wording' rule applies to ביטול רשות and rules out any courtyard-to-courtyard renunciation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule was said about the מבוי משנה, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the main topic: שמואל says there is no ביטול רשות from one courtyard to another, and none in a חורבה. רבי יוחנן says there is in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself. שמואל said: There is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another, and there is no giving up of rights in a ruin. And רבי יוחנן said: There is giving up of rights from one courtyard to another, and there is giving up of rights in a ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main statement of שמואל that was quoted earlier. It now shows that רבי יוחנן disagrees on both points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are argued. First, giving up rights between two courtyards. Second, giving up rights in an abandoned ruin between two houses. שמואל says no to both, and רבי יוחנן says yes to both.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; returning to a statement quoted earlier in order to study it
Giving up one's rights in a shared area so others can carry there
A ruin; an abandoned plot between houses

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core argument that the rest of the סוגיא analyzes.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Shmuel said:
There is no renunciation of rights from courtyard to courtyard,
and there is no renunciation of rights in a ruin.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is renunciation of rights from courtyard to courtyard,
and there is renunciation of rights in a ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to שמואל's base statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: no ביטול רשות between courtyards or in a חורבה. רבי יוחנן: yes in both.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed: the first half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why both cases had to be stated. If only the courtyard case were taught, we might think שמואל agrees with רבי יוחנן about a חורבה, since both neighbors use it together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary to state both. Suppose it had taught us only 'from courtyard to courtyard.' Then we would say שמואל said his rule in that case, because each courtyard has its own separate use. But a ruin has one shared use for both neighbors, so I would say שמואל agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכא, explaining why the argument had to be stated in both cases. The other half comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two courtyards are each used separately, so it makes sense that one cannot hand rights to the other. A חורבה is used by both neighbors together, so giving up rights there seems more natural. That is why we needed שמואל to say his rule about the חורבה explicitly.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: an explanation of why two similar statements are both needed
Use; how a space is used
Separately, on its own
Agrees, concedes

steps.confusionAlert: This is only half of the צריכא. The reverse argument, why the courtyard case is needed if the חורבה case is known, comes in the next step (Step 11).

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if it had taught us only 'from courtyard to courtyard,'
in this case Shmuel says his rule,
because this one has its use separately
and that one has its use separately.
But a ruin, where there is one use for both of them,
I would say: he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the argument in step 9 had to be stated in both cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The courtyard case alone would not teach the חורבה case, because a חורבה is shared in use and might allow ביטול רשות even for שמואל.

steps.title: Why the Ruin Case Alone Would Not Be Enough
steps.stepSummary: If only the חורבה case had been taught, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל about courtyards. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the argument had been stated only about the ruin, we would have said: only in this case does רבי יוחנן allow ביטול רשות, but in the other case (courtyard to courtyard) he agrees with שמואל. Therefore both cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the 'why did we need both cases' discussion from step 10. It now gives the other side: the חורבה case alone could have misled us about רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed that the courtyard case alone could mislead us about שמואל. Here, the חורבה case alone could mislead us about רבי יוחנן. We might think he allows ביטול only in a ruin, which both neighbors use together, and not between two separate courtyards. So each case teaches something the other could not teach.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. This is the conclusion of a צריכותא, which explains why two similar statements were both needed.
He agrees (concedes)
In that (other) case

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל says no ביטול in both a courtyard and a חורבה. רבי יוחנן says ביטול works in both. Each case had to be stated so we would not wrongly think either side gives in on one of them.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in this case (the ruin),
we would say: only in this case does Rabbi Yochanan say his view,
phrases.notes: Because a ruin is used by both neighbors together, ביטול seems more reasonable there.

phrases.english: but in the other case (courtyard to courtyard) he agrees with Shmuel.
Therefore it is necessary (to state both).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִתְּמַר בְּהָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 10 by giving the reverse side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the courtyard case and the חורבה case are needed to show the full positions of שמואל and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: אביי Limits שמואל's Rule to Side-by-Side Courtyards
steps.stepSummary: אביי says שמואל's 'no ביטול between courtyards' rule applies only to two side-by-side courtyards with one opening between them. If one courtyard is inside the other, ביטול is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When שמואל said there is no ביטול רשות from one courtyard to another, he meant only two courtyards with one doorway between them. But with two courtyards where one is inside the other, since they make each other forbidden, they may also do ביטול for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets a limit on שמואל's rule. He explains exactly which kind of courtyards שמואל was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With side-by-side courtyards, each one has its own exit to the alley, so neither one forbids the other. That is why ביטול does not apply there. When one courtyard is inside the other, the inner residents must walk through the outer one, so they forbid each other. Since they cause each other's problem, they can also fix it through ביטול רשות.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only in the case of... (a phrase that limits a rule)
One inside the other (the inner courtyard can only be reached through the outer one)
Since they forbid each other, they can also do ביטול for each other
One doorway between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל bans ביטול between all courtyards. According to אביי, his rule covers only side-by-side courtyards that do not forbid each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key rule of thumb: whoever can make you forbidden can also release their rights to you.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That which Shmuel said,
'there is no renouncing of rights from courtyard to courtyard,'
we said this only
about two courtyards with one doorway between them,
phrases.notes: These are side-by-side courtyards, each with its own exit to the alley.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ,
phrases.english: but with two courtyards, one inside the other,
since they forbid each other, they may renounce their rights.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל אֵין בִּיטּוּל רְשׁוּת מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר, לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the צריכותא ends, a new line opens that defines the exact scope of שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's ban on ביטול applies only to side-by-side courtyards. Courtyards one inside the other may do ביטול, since they forbid each other.

steps.title: רבא: Inner and Outer Courtyards Do Not Always Allow Renouncing
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even with one courtyard inside the other, ביטול sometimes works and sometimes does not. He begins his cases: if the עירוב was placed in the outer courtyard and anyone forgot to join, both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even with two courtyards, one inside the other, sometimes they may do ביטול and sometimes they may not. How so? If they put their עירוב in the outer courtyard, and one person forgot to join, whether from the inner or the outer courtyard, both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי's simple rule. He starts listing cases to show that inner and outer courtyards do not always work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that courtyards one inside the other can always do ביטול. רבא says it depends on the details. He starts with this case: the shared עירוב sits in the outer courtyard. If even one person from either courtyard did not join, the joint עירוב fails and the outer courtyard is forbidden. Since the inner residents' עירוב is located in that forbidden outer courtyard, they are left with no working עירוב at all, so the inner courtyard is forbidden too.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inner and outer courtyards do not always allow ביטול. If the עירוב is in the outer courtyard and anyone forgets to join, both courtyards are forbidden.

steps.title: רבא's Next Case: עירוב in the Inner Courtyard, Inner Resident Forgot
steps.stepSummary: If the עירוב was placed in the inner courtyard and an inner resident forgot to join, both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they placed their עירוב in the inner courtyard, and one person from the inner courtyard forgot and did not join, both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his list of cases. He now moves the עירוב to the inner courtyard and looks at what happens when someone from the inner courtyard forgets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inner resident who did not join makes the inner courtyard itself forbidden. The inner residents walk through the outer courtyard, so the problem spreads there too, and both courtyards are forbidden. Notice that רבא says only 'from the inner courtyard' here. This hints that a forgetful outer resident may lead to a different result.

phrases.notes: The inner courtyard is forbidden because of him. Since the inner residents pass through the outer courtyard, it is forbidden too.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the עירוב is in the inner courtyard and an inner resident forgets to join, both courtyards are forbidden.

steps.title: Inner-courtyard עירוב where an outer resident forgot: inner permitted, outer forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא's final case: the עירוב was placed in the inner courtyard and a resident of the outer courtyard forgot to join. The inner courtyard is permitted and the outer courtyard is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one person from the outer courtyard forgot and did not join the עירוב, the inner courtyard is permitted and the outer courtyard is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the last case on his list. The עירוב is still in the inner courtyard, as in Step 14, but this time the person who forgot lives in the outer courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who forgot makes his own outer courtyard forbidden. The inner courtyard stays permitted, because outer residents have no right to walk through the inner courtyard, so they cannot make it forbidden. This is the one case where the result is split: one courtyard is permitted and the other is forbidden.

steps.title: Restating the outer-courtyard עירוב case to explain why ביטול fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבא's first case: the עירוב was placed in the outer courtyard and anyone forgot, so both courtyards are forbidden. It repeats it in order to explain why ביטול can't help.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they placed their עירוב in the outer courtyard and one person forgot, whether from the inner or the outer courtyard, and did not join, both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the case from Step 13. This step is a setup: next, the גמרא will explain why the person who forgot cannot simply give up his rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who forgot to join the עירוב can do ביטול רשות, giving up his rights so that the others may carry. The גמרא now wants to show why that normal fix does not work here. Repeating the case sets up a short analysis of each possible ביטול.

steps.title: An inner resident who forgot has no one he can give up his rights to
steps.stepSummary: If the person who forgot is from the inner courtyard, giving up his rights to the inner residents doesn't help, because their עירוב is not with them. Giving them up to the outer residents isn't allowed, because there is no ביטול from one courtyard to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: This inner resident: to whom should he give up his rights? Let him give them up to the inner residents? Their עירוב is not with them. Let him give them up to the outer residents? There is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks both people this inner resident might give up his rights to, and shows that both options fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1 is the inner residents. Their עירוב food sits in the outer courtyard, so his ביטול in their favor doesn't give them a working עירוב where they are. Option 2 is the outer residents. That is blocked by שמואל's rule that ביטול cannot pass from one courtyard to another. So no ביטול is possible, and both courtyards stay forbidden.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how strong a limit שמואל's rule is: once ביטול across courtyards is ruled out, there is often no way left to fix the problem.

steps.title: An outer resident who forgot has no one he can give up his rights to
steps.stepSummary: If the person who forgot is from the outer courtyard, giving up his rights to the outer residents doesn't help, because the inner courtyard still makes them forbidden. Giving them up to the inner residents crosses courtyards, which isn't allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This outer resident: to whom should he give up his rights? Let him give them up to the outer residents? There is still the inner courtyard that makes them forbidden. Let him give them up to the inner residents? There is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same test for the outer resident who forgot, and again both options fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1 is the outer residents. Even after his ביטול, the inner courtyard is still a problem: its residents walk through the outer courtyard and their shared עירוב is broken, so they still make the outer courtyard forbidden. Option 2 is the inner residents, which is blocked by שמואל's rule against ביטול across courtyards.

steps.stepSummary: Giving up his rights to the inner residents doesn't help, because the outer courtyard still makes them forbidden. Giving them up to the outer residents crosses courtyards. So both courtyards stay forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This inner resident: to whom should he give up his rights? Let him give them up to the inner residents? There is still the outer courtyard that makes them forbidden. Let him give them up to the outer residents? There is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another.

Their עירוב is with them now, but the outer courtyard still makes them forbidden, because the shared עירוב gives outer residents rights in the inner courtyard. Option 2 is the outer residents, which is blocked again by שמואל's rule. So every case on רבא's list where both courtyards are forbidden comes down to that same rule.

steps.whatToRemember: In every case where both courtyards are forbidden, the person who forgot has two choices for ביטול, and both fail. Either a courtyard still makes things forbidden, or the ביטול would cross courtyards, which שמואל says is impossible (אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר). That is רבא's point: even with one courtyard inside the other, ביטול does not always help.
